key_insight: The paper shows that how you choose the reference report can significantly change the measured quality of chest X-ray report generation systems. In short, evaluation is not just about the model—it is also about the reporting style used as the benchmark.
problem_solved: It addresses the mismatch between heterogeneous radiology reporting practices and the way AI-generated reports are evaluated. Different valid radiologist reports can describe the same findings differently, making standard reference-based evaluation unreliable.
method: Analyzes variability in real radiologist chest X-ray reports, including differences in terminology, shorthand, formatting, and detail level.
Examines how different reference choices affect automatic and human evaluation of radiology report generation models.
Highlights the need for evaluation protocols that account for multiple acceptable reference styles rather than assuming a single gold-standard report.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means report generation scores may be misleading if the reference report is stylistically different from the model output. Better evaluation design can lead to fairer benchmarking and more trustworthy progress in medical NLP and radiology AI.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of two valid radiology reports describing the same image with different wording
Flow diagram showing how reference choice changes evaluation scores
Bar chart comparing model performance under different reporting styles
Icon set representing terminology, shorthand, formatting, and detail variation
paper_title: Reporting Practice Matters: The Impact of Reference Choice on Chest X-ray Report Evaluation
paper_authors: Daniel P. Jeong, Charles Q. Li, Hossein Hosseiny, Nitya M. Bhalla, Fatma Uyar Morency
